UKRAINE VS RUSSIA - THE SCENE, THE FALL OUT, THE FUTURE

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We take a look at the brewing tension between Ukraine and Russia and ask what it means for South Africa.

Unique Selling Point:
** CURRENT AFFAIRS - WE ARE IN IT AS IT HAPPENS

Summary:
With threats of a Russian invasion mounting, Ukrainians gear up and buckle down as their allies get ready to send in support to fight off Putin's forces.



Further information:
Four main areas:
1. How did we get here
2. What’s next
3. The weighing up contradictory intelligence
4. A South African context perspective - why should we care?

INTERVIEWS
1. Paul Nilan - a businessman, writer, and political commentator. His passion for Ukraine stems from his involvement in the revolutions of 2004/5 and 2013/4, and his writings about Ukraine are often focused on helping the international community better understand the reasons for and background behind the ongoing war in the Donbas, as well as Ukraine in general.

ZOOM INTERVIEW AND WHATSAPP CALL WALKABOUT KIYV

2. JOHN STREMLAU - Honorary Professor, International Relations, at Wits
Prof Stremlau publishes extensively on foreign affairs and is a frequent media commentator on international network news programmes - he has been critical of the South AFrican government and warns against the world playing into Putin's games.

ZOOM INTERVIEW - NOT HAPPY IN TIMES OF COVID TO MEET FACE TO FACE - JOKED THAT HE's OLD NOW

3. UKRAINIAN AMBASSADOR - Liubov Abravitova

FINAL SCRIPT: UKRAINE VS RUSSIA

ADD IN VISUAL BREATHING SPACE – 2 SECONDS
VO: Talks of an invasion, a show of military force and the potential for global conflict – this was the scene in Eastern Europe this week.

PUTIN: do we want war? or not? Of course not

VO: But actions speak louder than words

UPSOUND – MISSILE // GUN FIRE

ZELENSKYY: We have to be ready each day, and it began not yesterday.

LINK: Every major news network has covered the standoff between Ukraine and Russia – while there is a lot of uncertainty – the one guarantee is that the repercussions of these wargames will be felt across the globe.

PROF: This is a throwback to the old era of big power politics - the opportunity costs for having this crisis are very, very high for countries like South Africa.

VO: In recent weeks, more than 150 000 Russian military troops moved within reach of Ukraine's borders.

NATO: This is the biggest concentration of forces in Europe since the Cold War.

VO: The build-up of military forces is an alarming development considering that Russia has already invaded Ukraine and seized its territory.

Professor John Stremlau specialises in International Relations.

PROF: in 2014, the people of Ukraine rose up in an orange revolution. and then Putin broke the rules by annexing Crimea, plus the fact that there is an insurgency among Russian peoples in the easternmost province of of Ukraine And that's where we are.

VO: These visuals released by the Russian Defence Ministry show active operations in full swing.

Alexander Arefiev is the Russian Embassy’s Press-Attache in Pretoria.

MASA: those visuals of the troops are just daunting
RUSSIA These are the only visuals of the troops of conducting military exercises. // If any other country conducts the entire exercise, that's fine with Russia. Why is not fine with everyone else when Russia conducts military exercises?
MASA: But it just seen as a sign of intimidation.
RUSSIA: We don't care if it's see if it seems like it, if someone sees it as a threat, it doesn't make it a threat.

VO: Western governments disagree.


The intergovernmental military alliance between a number of Western countries and North America - NATO - is gearing up for a worst case scenario.

NATO: We have already enhanced our deterrence and defence. With more troops, planes and ships. And higher readiness of the NATO Response Force. These steps are defensive. //

VO: Although becoming part of NATO is a process that could take years, Ukraine is keen to join - and Russia, is not happy about it.

RUSSIA: Why would they want to join NATO in the first place?
MASA: But it's their choice, whether they want to or not?
RUSSIA: No, no. It's the exact answer for security security purposes.
MAS: but it's their choice. M6
RUSSIA: Well, Russia has the right to defend itselfM6

LINK: The whole world is waiting with bated breath for this imminent invasion – but for Ukrainians this is nothing new. Paul Niland is a political commentator that’s lived in Ukraine for 19 years – Paul, thanks for agreeing to show us around – what’s it’s like living there right now?

PAUL: It's just an ordinary day. The threat of invasion is 350 kilometers from here. we know the threat. But at the same time, we can't let that change the way that we live. we've adapted.
MASA: WOULD YOU BE READY FOR A POTENTIAL STRIKE
PAUL: Any city where potentially Russia might decide to send in an occupation army, there will be a civilian resistance.

VO: While Russia claims NATO is a direct threat to it, the organisation denies this.

NATO: NATO is not a threat to Russia. And we have no plans, in a way, to deploy offensive systems in Ukraine.

VO: LIUBOV ABRAVITOVA is the UKRANIAN AMBASSADOR to South Africa.

UKRAINE: What makes Russia to feel themselves unsafe? No one is making a buildup on their border. No one. And the appearance of Ukraine on the map of the NATO doesn't bring from my humble opinion any threat to Russia. NATO's already close to Russia for many years.
MASA: To tell you, as Ukraine, a sovereign state, what to do.
UKRAINE: Russia want Ukraine politically, economically to control it. This is the main issue.

PROF: There is a racial dimension to this that no one seems to mention. //He's striding around like a like a conquering colonialist.

LINK: As the world weighed in, South Africa has stayed on the sidelines //

MINISTER: IN the ukraine russia tension that is clearly being exploited by those who are hostile to Russia for the purpose of once again unjustifiably extending spheres of influence, we urge calm and restraint.

LINK: [MASA SWITCHES TV OFF]: NOT GETTING ACTIVELY… A MOVE THAT HAS NOT GONE UNNOTICED

PROF: It's more a question of what South Africans think about their role in the world and who they speak for or against. At the moment, South Africa is the only liberal democracy in the BRICS. // it does owe it to itself to stand up for its values, I think. M17

VO: The world is interconnected. With Russia being a major global supplier of gas and petroleum, the economic cost of an invasion will reach far beyond its borders and the humanitarian impact could be devastating to the region.

LINK: A number of countries have called on their citizens to leave, as tension mounts in the region. Yet Russia implies the situation has been blown out of proportion…

RUSSIA: There is no invasion, there is no invasion.
MASA: So this is all just hysteria that's been made up.
RUSSIA: Exactly. No one's looking for war. But yet the US and UK instigating, they say that Russia is going to invade.

VO: By Tuesday this week, Russia announced a partial withdrawal of its forces near the Ukraine border. While some footage of the pullback was released - not everyone is convinced.

PAUL: One of the important principles when dealing with Russia is everything must be verified. If we look at their track record, they don't. They don't warrant our goodwill of taking them at face value.

RUSSIA: What Russia does in its own territory. That's Russia's concern. Some of those troops have been withdrawn //some did not complete their objective yet of the military drills //

VO: Subsequent Satellite images showed that some Russian military equipment was moved, but it also appears that there is a new build-up of amoured vehicles, helicopters and artillery.

Then on Thursday, projectile missiles were fired - hitting a kindergarten in the disputed Eastern region of Ukraine. The suspected intention is to create a pretext for the two countries going to war.

MASA: Is there a possibility that Ukraine would be willing to drop its plans to join NATO for some sort of a solution?
UKRAINE: Do you think it would be a good signal for all the world that under this pressure, militarily pressure the country can give up the sovereign right to choose its way?

VO: Despite the so-called exercises on the ground, Russia maintains it open to a diplomatic solution

RUSSIA:we see that diplomacy is the best option for everyone. // There is no such thing as Russia invasion. It's just absurd

VO: But Ukrainians are still sceptical.

PAUL: if there is no invasion immediately, the threat of the invasion is going to rear its ugly head again. //Putin is not finished with his ambitions in Ukraine.

VO: A sentiment shared by Western Countries - the risk of an invasion is still high.


PROMOS

PROMO 1 – 21 seconds
VO: As tension mounts in Eastern Europe – the world watches as the risk of a global conflict runs high

PROF: // This is a throwback to the old era of big power politics,M4 //.

UPSOUND GUNS `& BOMBS

NATO: This is the biggest concentration of forces in Europe since the Cold War.




PROMO 2 – 21 seconds
VO: A show of military force, An imminent invasion and conflicting intelligence fuel global panic.

UPSOUND BOOM

PAUL: // any city where potentially Russia might decide to send in an occupation army, there will be a civilian resistance.

VO: As military forces gear up, the world watches as Eastern Europe buckles down.




PROMO 3 – 11 seconds
VO: It’s the biggest concentration of military forces in Europe since the Cold War - it’s a stand off between Russia and Ukraine. - But what does it mean for South AFrica and the globe.
